The app and the keyboard cannot share settings yet. Rebuild the app so the App Group entitlement is applied.
Changes the language of this app. The keyboard\'s own labels follow the layout you select on the keyboard itself.

Tapping %1$s sends the message you copied or selected and your instruction; %2$s sends only your instruction. With Smart correction on, an instruction you type in AI\u00A0Reply\'s own field may also be sent to suggest a correction. Text goes through the AI\u00A0Reply server to OpenAI and is not stored in the database or written to logs, except the text of a report you choose to send.
Keyboard status, step-by-step setup and how AI\u00A0Reply reads what you copy.
The shared container is unavailable, so the keyboard cannot see your profile. Rebuild the app with the App Group capability enabled.
iOS does not tell an app whether its own keyboard is enabled. This turns green the first time the keyboard runs.
Only you can turn it on, in Settings ▸ General ▸ Keyboard ▸ Keyboards ▸ AI Reply. No app can enable it for you.
Full Access lets the keyboard read the message you copied and reach the internet to write a reply. Without it the keyboard still types normally.
When iOS asks for permission to paste copied text, choose Allow. The keyboard only processes text you explicitly copied.
iOS shows that prompt itself, and only when the keyboard reads the clipboard after you tap a template.
The clipboard is never monitored in the background.
Copied text is read only when you tap a template or the paste button, and a reply is generated only when you tap Reply.
Your sign-in tokens are kept in protected app storage and are not shown in the keyboard.
Passwords and secure fields are never processed.
Voice input uses Android speech recognition. Availability and whether audio is processed on device depend on your device and selected recognition service.
iOS only lets an app open its own settings page, so the keyboard list has to be opened by hand.
Add the keyboard in iPhone Settings to generate contextual replies in messaging apps.
Name your template, for example Supplier or Close Friend.

A short walkthrough: copy a message, reply from the keyboard, practise. Nothing is reset.

Android warns that a keyboard “may be able to collect all the text you type”. Every keyboard gets this standard notice. AI\u00A0Reply sends text through its server to OpenAI when you tap %1$s or %2$s and, with Smart correction on, the instruction you type in its own field, to suggest a correction. Nothing else you type is sent.
